purpose: Track the technologies and companies that make enterprise AI possible, with the emphasis on architecture and career learning rather than stock selection.

companies.role: Microsoft Foundry provides the enterprise management plane for agents, models, tools, identity, policy, networking, evaluation, and observability.
companies.career: Directly relevant to AI Platform Engineering: Foundry resources/projects, Entra identity, RBAC, private networking, Azure Policy, agent operations, monitoring, and governance.
companies.marketContext: Represents the enterprise cloud and AI platform layer where infrastructure is exposed as governed services to engineering teams.

companies.role: Provides high-density AI-ready colocation and private interconnection across clouds, networks, partners, and distributed infrastructure.
companies.career: Useful for understanding hybrid AI architecture, data locality, private connectivity, latency, colocation, cloud adjacency, and where enterprise workloads physically meet cloud AI services.
companies.marketContext: Represents the physical and connectivity layer that links enterprise data, private infrastructure, and public cloud AI services.

companies.role: Builds Ethernet networking platforms and EOS software for large AI clusters, including rack-scale 800G and 1.6T fabrics.
companies.career: Teaches scale-out Ethernet, RDMA/RoCE, telemetry, deterministic network performance, congestion behavior, fabric operations, and why network design controls accelerator utilization.
companies.marketContext: Represents independent AI-fabric networking and the operational software required to run high-bandwidth clusters.

companies.role: Supplies AI networking, connectivity silicon, and custom accelerators used in large-scale AI clusters.
companies.career: Useful for understanding scale-up versus scale-out networks, custom XPUs, switching silicon, interconnect bottlenecks, and why hyperscalers increasingly co-design compute and networking.
companies.marketContext: Represents the networking-silicon and custom-accelerator layer behind hyperscale AI infrastructure.

companies.role: Combines accelerated compute with NVLink scale-up, Spectrum-X Ethernet, InfiniBand, BlueField DPUs, and infrastructure software for AI factories.
companies.career: A compact way to study the whole GPU system: accelerators, scale-up links, scale-out fabrics, DPUs, telemetry, infrastructure offload, and multi-data-center AI networking.
companies.marketContext: Represents the accelerated-compute platform plus the networking stack required to keep large GPU systems utilized.

companies.role: GPU systems provide the accelerated compute foundation for large-scale AI training and inference.
companies.career: Learn GPU cluster architecture, scale-up versus scale-out, utilization, power and cooling constraints, workload placement, and the operational dependencies below model hosting.
companies.marketContext: Represents the compute layer that turns models into running workloads.

companies.role: HBM and data-center memory keep accelerators supplied with the bandwidth and capacity required by AI workloads.
companies.career: Build intuition for memory bandwidth, capacity, data movement, accelerator starvation, power efficiency, and why AI performance is a system problem rather than only a GPU problem.
companies.marketContext: Represents the memory layer that determines how quickly accelerators can access model weights and active data.

companies.role: Advanced semiconductor manufacturing plus CoWoS and 3DFabric packaging integrates logic, chiplets, and HBM into high-performance AI systems.
companies.career: Explains why packaging, yield, interposer size, chiplets, HBM integration, thermals, and manufacturing capacity matter to the infrastructure layer above them.
companies.marketContext: Represents the manufacturing and packaging foundation underneath accelerators, networking silicon, and memory integration.

signals.title: Foundry continues consolidating agents, models, tools, RBAC, networking, policy, evaluation, and observability into one enterprise platform surface.
signals.careerTakeaway: Study the control plane: identity, project isolation, RBAC, networking, diagnostics, and managed agent execution.

signals.title: Arista introduced a 1.6T Etherlink portfolio aimed at rack-scale AI infrastructure and scale-up / scale-out fabrics.
signals.careerTakeaway: AI platform reliability increasingly depends on understanding RDMA fabrics, high-speed Ethernet, telemetry, power, and thermals.

signals.title: Micron lists HBM4 in high-volume production with more than 2.8 TB/s bandwidth per stack.
signals.careerTakeaway: Memory bandwidth is a first-class AI infrastructure constraint; GPU count alone does not explain system performance.

signals.title: TSMC positions CoWoS as a core foundation for HPC and AI by integrating compute logic with HBM and continuing to scale packaging capacity.
signals.careerTakeaway: Advanced packaging is part of AI infrastructure architecture because compute density, memory bandwidth, thermals, and supply all meet at the package level.

Hybrid AI interconnection and data locality
